event.title: Thunderstorms to Clear Wildfire Smoke Ahead of World Cup Final
event.canonical_title: Thunderstorms to Clear Wildfire Smoke Ahead of World Cup Final
event.summary: Meteorologists predict that thunderstorms will help clear wildfire smoke from the Northeast United States ahead of the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina. The storm front is expected to move the smoke out of the region, improving air quality for the event. However, warnings of unhealthy air quality remain in effect across a wide area.

timeline.title: Thunderstorms to Clear Wildfire Smoke Ahead of World Cup Final
timeline.summary: Thunderstorms are expected to clear wildfire smoke from the Northeast United States before the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina. While the storm front has largely moved the smoke out of the Northeast, some smoke remains over the central US Warnings for unhealthy air quality are still in effect across a wide area.
key_facts: Thunderstorms will clear wildfire smoke from the Northeast.
The World Cup final is between Spain and Argentina.
Some smoke lingers over the central United States.
Warnings for unhealthy air quality remain in effect.
